title: Bristol Stool Chart Guide
subtitle: Understand stool consistency and its meaning for your UC
selectPrompt: Tap any card to select it directly into your daily log

headerTip.title: How to interpret this in Ulcerative Colitis?
headerTip.desc: Type 4 is the gold standard for clinical remission (calmed, healed mucosa). Types 6 & 7 indicate rapid colonic transit caused by active inflammation, requiring hydration and symptom tracking.

type1.title: Type 1: Separate hard lumps
type1.shapeDesc: Hard, dry little balls resembling nuts, difficult to pass and requiring straining.
type1.clinicalMeaning: Severe constipation. The colon has absorbed nearly all water. May cause straining and fissures.
type1.actionTip: Increase your daily fluid intake and speak with your GI doctor regarding safe soluble fibers for UC.

type2.title: Type 2: Lumpy sausage-shaped
type2.shapeDesc: Firm cylindrical mass with multiple compacted lumps and an irregular surface.
type2.clinicalMeaning: Mild constipation. Compacted stool indicating prolonged passage through the large intestine.
type2.actionTip: Maintain steady hydration throughout the day and avoid delaying bowel movement urges.

type3.title: Type 3: Sausage-shaped with cracks
type3.shapeDesc: Long sausage shape with shallow surface fissures, passing easily without strain.
type3.clinicalMeaning: Healthy, balanced consistency. Indicates proper nutrient absorption and adequate hydration.
type3.actionTip: Excellent consistency. Continue with your regular diet and prescribed maintenance medication.

type4.title: Type 4: Smooth, soft snake or sausage
type4.shapeDesc: Soft, smooth sausage or snake shape. Slides out effortlessly with zero pain.
type4.clinicalMeaning: Ideal! Represents the clinical goal of UC remission, reflecting a calmed, healthy colonic mucosa.
type4.actionTip: Goal achieved! Maintain strict adherence to your prescribed UC maintenance treatment.

type5.title: Type 5: Soft blobs with clear-cut edges
type5.shapeDesc: Soft pasty pieces with distinct, well-defined borders that pass easily.
type5.clinicalMeaning: Tendency toward diarrhea. The colon is accelerating stool passage before full water reabsorption.
type5.actionTip: Monitor whether consistency turns more liquid in subsequent episodes and reinforce hydration.

type6.title: Type 6: Fluffy, mushy pieces with ragged edges
type6.shapeDesc: Pasty, shapeless stool with torn, ragged fragments and lacking solid form.
type6.clinicalMeaning: Mild to moderate diarrhea. Common during UC inflammation flare-ups or food intolerances.
type6.actionTip: Avoid processed or irritating foods, hydrate with water and electrolyte drinks, and track blood/mucus.

type7.title: Type 7: Watery, entirely liquid with no solids
type7.shapeDesc: Completely watery and fluid consistency, with no solid chunks whatsoever.
type7.clinicalMeaning: Severe diarrhea / Inflammatory hyperactivity. The inflamed mucosa cannot retain water.
type7.actionTip: Dehydration alert! Drink oral rehydration salts/coconut water. Contact your GI doctor if it persists.
